title: Scoreboard Explorer
lede: The always-on Scoreboard now turns Schedule history into reusable, trustworthy combinations—the stat engine for a future end-of-year story without naming the current year in the product.

stats.n: Sport, Schedule venue, opponent, and site
Unchanged bounded event reads; no per-person N+1

sections.heading: From one filter to a stat explorer
sections.note: Matched 1440 × 1000 authenticated captures use the same Admin, Preview data, dark theme, and page shell. The baseline is the previously accepted team Scoreboard captured earlier on August 23; the new capture changes only this feature slice.

pairs.title: All-events Scoreboard
pairs.sub: The full current window remains the default, but its reusable dimensions and story layer are now explicit.
pairs.beforeCap: Before: one Sport select, a year-named badge, and totals that led directly into the leaderboard.
pairs.afterCap: After: four stable dimensions, generic Current season copy, and a deterministic Snapshot naming the current story and most-events contributor.

sections.heading: Every combination becomes its own story
sections.note: These are two states of the same new build and viewport. Selecting a row or menu value changes one exact dimension; clearing it preserves the rest of the stack.

pairs.title: Three filters, one intersection
pairs.sub: The totals, Snapshot, leaderboard, and every breakdown agree on Volleyball at UW Field House against Butler.
pairs.beforeCap: All events: 15 covered, 3–2 official record, 45 work credits, and 16 contributors.
pairs.afterCap: Stacked view: one covered event, 0–0 official record, three work credits, three contributors, and a matching three-person leaderboard.

changes.h: A sport filter could not answer venue or matchup questions
changes.was: The aggregate view could narrow only by sport, so records at a venue, against a team, or by Home/Away/Neutral site required a different surface or mental arithmetic.
changes.now: Sport, Schedule venue, opponent, and site are first-class exact dimensions. One value per dimension stacks with AND semantics on both web and native.

changes.h: Independent numbers could drift into different scopes
changes.was: Adding dimensions client-side would risk filtering the team record without filtering work totals or person rankings the same way.
changes.now: The server filters the two bounded event sets once, then derives totals, four breakdowns, and every person summary from that shared intersection.

changes.h: Narrowing could collapse the next menu
changes.was: If filter choices came from the current result, selecting one dimension could make valid choices in another disappear and strand the user.
changes.now: Facets always come from the complete bounded window. Empty intersections are recoverable, and removing one filter leaves every other selection intact.

changes.h: The numbers had no narrative layer
changes.was: A reader could inspect totals, but the interface did not name the particular combination or surface its leading contributor as a reusable fact.
changes.now: Snapshot turns every current intersection into a compact, deterministic story—the first presentation layer for future recap cards, superlatives, and streaks.

verification: Focused contracts: 110 tests across 15 web, API, RBAC, navigation, and native-source Vitest files pass.
Static and build gates: TypeScript, full ESLint, npm run build:app, XcodeGen project sync, and the pinned iPhone 16 Pro iOS 26.5 build pass.
Native models: focused ScoreboardModelsTests complete successfully against additive and older response fixtures.

Authenticated browser: real Preview data rendered four stable facets; Volleyball + UW Field House + Butler returned one event and three matching contributors; an impossible Football combination rendered the recoverable empty state; browser console errors were empty.
Docs and repository hygiene: codemaps, docs verification, and git diff --check pass.
notes: Production was not changed. The installed signed-in native build reaches the canonical host, which still returns 404 for the undeployed aggregate route; live native totals and filter interaction remain a post-deploy GAP-71 gate.
Venue is the cleaned Schedule venue derived from raw calendar location text, never an equipment pickup location. Site is the canonical Home/Away/Neutral event classification.

The future end-of-year experience is product direction, not shipped scope here. Any superlative, streak, or surprising combination must remain reproducible from the same event authority, counting rules, and privacy allowlist.
No schema, migration, commit, push, deployment, or public Scoreboard publishing was performed.
